reporter_ref: maintainer instruction 2026-10-14: set kDexCohortFloor to 1, ride-along on this change
adjudicated_by: maintainer ruling 2026-10-14 (absolute, not for relitigation); applied by the change author, who did not make the ruling
adjudication_rationale: The repository maintainer ruled that kDexCohortFloor is one device: a cohort, point or figure is published whenever at least one device contributed, and suppression only ever marks an empty point or cohort. Every consumer derives from the one constant, so the fleet, management-group and device-tag app-performance trends, the fleet cohort benchmarks and head-to-head diff, the per-device cohort comparison strip, the per-version crash and hang join, the Apps list stability figures and VERIFY's small_cohort flag all follow it. The rate-ratio exposure guard (kDexRateRatioMinExposure) follows too (one exposure unit per arm): it protects the division, not identity, and the exact conditional interval carries a thin arm's uncertainty. The wire is additive: suppressed, small_cohort, the floor echo and the below_floor withheld token stay; nothing is removed.
waiver_rationale: Accepted residual under the ruling: a point or cohort covering a single device, including a named management-group or device-model cohort of one, now publishes that device's exact CPU/memory aggregate on the un-audited app-performance and cohort reads. Bounds: fleet-wide aggregates by application, version or cohort value only; no agent_id or device identifier on any of them; every read behind the access-reviewed GuaranteedState:Read; the audited per-device drill remains the individual path. Stated in the SOC 2 exemption paragraph, the routed Guardian/DEX row, the REST reference and the changelog.
reporter: security-guardian (the privacy consequence as the domain reporter would derive it; the ruling itself is the maintainer's)
trigger: kDexCohortFloor set from 10 to 1, so the statistical floor no longer withholds a one-to-nine-device aggregate on any DEX app-performance or cohort read
classification_rationale: the routed row, the SOC 2 exemption sentence, the statistics and score banners, the OpenAPI and MCP descriptions and the manuals all stated a floor of 10 and a 2026-10-14 exception; every one is reworded in this change to state the one-device floor and its consequence
summary: Maintainer ruling applied: the cohort floor is one device on every DEX surface that derives from kDexCohortFloor. Proven by tests that fail against the old value (floored helpers at one device, a scored one-device population, three-device points published on the fleet, group and tag paths over REST, MCP and the dashboard fragment, a four-device cohort benchmarked, a three-device cohort diffed, small_cohort false at three paired machines). The privacy residual is accepted under the ruling and recorded here and in the SOC 2 policy line.

adjudicated_by: maintainer ruling 2026-10-14 (absolute, not for relitigation); the statements were corrected by the change author after governance review
adjudication_rationale: Supersedes the pass-1 row: its bounds sentence omitted two channels the code opens at a one-device floor. The floor ruling itself is unchanged and is not re-adjudicated; only the persisted statement of its consequence was inexact.
waiver_rationale: Accepted residual under the ruling: a point or cohort covering a single device, including a named management-group, device-model or device-tag cohort of one, publishes that device's exact CPU/memory aggregate. A cohort label is the operator tag value, so a cohort keyed by a per-device tag value (an asset tag, serial number or owner) is that device's exact figures, returned on the un-audited tag, cohort and Apps reads; the audited per-device drill is not the only route to per-device figures. The opt-in Prometheus cohort export puts the same figures on /metrics, which is bounded by the /metrics authentication setting and the admin-gated export key, not by GuaranteedState:Read. Bounds that do hold: aggregates by application, version or cohort value only, no agent_id on any API, MCP or dashboard read, and every API, MCP and dashboard read behind the access-reviewed GuaranteedState:Read. Stated in the SOC 2 exemption paragraph and risk register, the routed Guardian/DEX row, the REST reference, the metrics reference, the upgrade note and the changelog.

adjudicated_by: maintainer ruling 2026-10-14 (absolute, not for relitigation); the statements were corrected by the change author after a second governance review
adjudication_rationale: Supersedes the pass-2 row: its waiver rationale was over-broad. The floor ruling itself is unchanged and is not re-adjudicated; only the persisted statement of its consequence is corrected.
waiver_rationale: Accepted residual under the ruling: a point or cohort covering a single device, including a named management-group, device-model or device-tag cohort of one, publishes that device's exact CPU/memory aggregate. There is no agent_id on the exempt aggregate reads; the audited per-device drills and the per-device list do name one. A cohort label is an operator- or agent-sourced tag value that may itself identify a device (an asset tag, serial number or owner), so a cohort keyed by a per-device tag value is that device's exact figures on the un-audited tag and cohort reads. The Apps list is keyed by application and version only, never by a tag value. The opt-in Prometheus cohort export puts the same figures on /metrics, which is bounded by the /metrics authentication setting (loopback is open; remote scrapes need any authenticated session) and the admin-gated export key, not by GuaranteedState:Read; the export cap bounds how many cohorts export, not how small they are. Stated in the SOC 2 exemption paragraph and risk register, the REST reference, the metrics reference, the upgrade note and the changelog.

reporter_ref: governance second review of the Apps stability read model
trigger: the persisted score policy that follows this change can fail to load, and DexScorePolicyFn returns a policy by value with no failure channel
classification_rationale: the provider type has no way to report a failed policy read; the builder already degrades on an invalid policy, so a failure can only be expressed as an invalid one today
summary: DexScorePolicyFn carries no failure channel. Deferred to the change that persists the policy: today the only provider is the in-process default, which cannot fail, so no reachable path is affected.

reporter_ref: governance second review of the Apps stability read model
trigger: a device alone in its cohort shows cohort size 1 and a percentile computed over one device
classification_rationale: the percentile is true but uninformative at a cohort of one; the floor ruling makes this the intended outcome rather than a defect
summary: A device alone in its cohort shows cohort size 1 and a true but uninformative percentile.
waiver_rationale: Accepted as a consequence of the one-device floor: the cohort size is shown beside the percentile, so a reader can see how much weight it carries.
